knowledge_point.title: Relating a Derivative to a Rate of Change

question.:question/problem:
A model records the number of items in a store at time $s$, measured in days after observations begin.

- $Q(s)$ - the number of items in a store, in items.

- $b(s)$ - the positive rate at which that amount is decreasing, in items per day.

What is the relationship between $Q(s)$ and $b(s)$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $Q(s)$ gives the number of items in a store after $s$ days. Then,

$$
Q'(s)=\frac{\text{d}Q(s)}{\text{d}s}=\frac{\text{Change in }Q}{\text{Change in }s}.
$$

Thus, $Q'(s)$ gives the instantaneous rate of change of that amount. The amount is decreasing, so the derivative is the negative of the positive loss rate $b(s)$. Therefore, the relationship is $Q'(s)=-b(s)$.

The change ratio denotes an instantaneous rate: the limit of change ratios as the time interval tends to zero.

question.:question/problem:
A model records the number of items in a store at time $s$, measured in days after observations begin.

- $Q(s)$ - the number of items in a store, in items.

- $B(s)$ - the positive rate at which the amount is added, in items per day.

What is the relationship between the three functions above?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $Q(s)$ gives the number of items in a store after $s$ days. Then,

$$
Q'(s)=\frac{\text{d}Q(s)}{\text{d}s}=\frac{\text{Change in }Q}{\text{Change in }s}.

In addition, we can compute this rate by finding the difference between the addition and removal rates at time $s$. That is,

$$
Q'(s)=B(s)-L(s).
$$

The change ratio denotes an instantaneous rate: the limit of change ratios as the time interval tends to zero.

What is the relationship between the three functions above?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The function $Q(s)$ gives the number of items in a store after $s$ days. Then,

$$
Q'(s)=\frac{\text{d}Q(s)}{\text{d}s}=\frac{\text{Change in }Q}{\text{Change in }s}.

$$
Q'(s)=B(s)+L(s).
$$

The change ratio denotes an instantaneous rate: the limit of change ratios as the time interval tends to zero.
